name: Puzzle
subtitle: Centered around information hiding and inference to create solution spaces; the core is learning curves and hint strategies.
demoRuleHint: Rule: Observe information → Perform action → Receive feedback → Infer next step → Achieve goal
problemsSolved: Clearly define objectives and actionable objects, avoiding the question 'What am I supposed to do?'
Use tiered hints to reduce frustration costs, encouraging players to keep trying.
Make trial-and-error feedback verifiable (correct/incorrect/progression), avoiding randomness and misdirection.
learningGoals: Understand how information disclosure guides learning curves.
Master the combination of 'single-step verification' and 'long-chain reasoning'.
Be able to design hints that are understandable without text.
minimalRules: Goal: satisfy conditions (minimum: reach endpoint / trigger mechanism).
Feedback: every step can be verified (correct / incorrect / neutral).
systemLoopHint: Input → Judgment → Feedback → State change → New input

combos.effect: Physics causal chains provide richer solution spaces.
Reconfiguring the state increases replayability, but explainability must be controlled.
Gradually unlock tools and rules, expanding reasoning ability.

advancedWarnings: Lack of verifiable feedback prevents players from assessing progress.
Too strong hints break the sense of achievement; too weak hints lead to abandonment.
When the solution is unique but the path is long, frustration is amplified.
Too many hints weaken the challenge; too few cause players to get lost—balancing information is the core design trade-off.
Excessive randomization can increase replayability but undermines causal chain explainability, making players feel purposeless.
Over-simplifying hints can actually increase curiosity—players will proactively try multiple strategies when lacking clues.
advancedAlgoRefs: Levels: solvability verification, solution search, hint generation
State: state machine / condition graph, used to express causal chains
